Welcome to LM Playground! I am committed to maintaining the trust and confidence of everyone who uses my app. This Privacy Policy explains what the app does and does not collect, how your conversations stay on your device, and the few cases — such as the optional web tools — where information leaves your device, so you always know what to expect.

I, Andriy Druk, the developer of LM Playground, do not collect, store, use, or share any personal information from the users of my app. There are no accounts, no advertising, and no usage analytics or tracking. The app is designed with your privacy as a priority, so you can use it without compromising your personal data.

Your conversations, system prompts, and the model\'s responses are processed locally on your device by the on-device model. This content is never sent to me or to any server for inference. It stays on your device unless you choose to use a feature that reaches the internet, as described below.

LM Playground requests Internet permission for two purposes: to download the model files you choose, and — only if you turn them on — to power the optional web tools. The app contains no advertising, telemetry, or usage analytics, and it does not report your activity back to me.

Capable models can use optional tools, which are turned off by default. When you enable the web tools, some information leaves your device: the Web search tool sends the model\'s search query to DuckDuckGo, and the Fetch web page tool downloads the pages the model decides to open from those websites. Those requests are handled by the third-party sites under their own privacy policies — I neither receive nor store them. The Run JavaScript tool runs entirely on your device in a sandbox with no internet access. To keep everything offline, simply leave the tools off.

As the developer of LM Playground, I reserve the right to update this Privacy Policy at any time. Any changes will be effective immediately upon posting the updated policy. Users are encouraged to review this page periodically and stay informed about how their privacy is protected.

By using LM Playground, you acknowledge and agree to this Privacy Policy. If you do not agree with the policy, please refrain from using the app. Your continued use of the app following the posting of any updates or changes to this policy will be deemed your acceptance of those changes.
If you have any questions or suggestions about my Privacy Policy, do not hesitate to contact me.
LM Playground lets you run large language models directly on your Android device. All processing happens locally \u2013 no cloud servers needed.
The app supports models in GGUF format with Q4_K_M quantization, including Qwen 3, Gemma 3, Llama 3.2, Phi\u20114 mini, and DeepSeek R1 Distill in various sizes.
How much storage space do I need?
Model sizes vary from about 500 MB (small models like Qwen 3 0.6B) to several GB (larger models like DeepSeek R1 7B). Make sure you have enough free space before downloading.
Does the app require an internet connection?

Internet is needed to download models, and — if you turn them on — for the optional web tools (web search and fetch page). Apart from that, once a model is downloaded it runs completely offline on your device.

Your conversations are processed locally on your device and are never sent to a server by the app. The one exception is the optional web tools: if you enable web search or fetch page, the model\'s search queries and the pages it opens are sent to those websites (search uses DuckDuckGo). Tools are off by default, so nothing leaves your device unless you turn them on. See the Privacy Policy for details.
Larger models take more time to load into memory. Loading times depend on your device\'s hardware. Once loaded, the model stays in memory until you unload it.
Devices with more RAM can run larger models. For best performance, use a device with at least 6 GB of RAM for small models and 8+ GB for larger ones.
Can I load a custom GGUF model?

Yes. Place your .gguf file in the storage folder selected in Settings \u2192 Models (the same folder used for downloads). The app will pick it up automatically and show it in the model selector alongside the built-in catalog. Chat template and tokenizer settings are read from the GGUF metadata. If a specific model doesn\'t work, please open an issue on GitHub.
Can I change where models are stored?
Yes. Go to Settings, then Models, and use the \u201CChange Folder\u201D option to select a different storage location.
How do I delete a model?
Go to Settings, then Models. In the \u201CDownloaded\u201D section, tap the delete icon next to the model you want to remove.

A system prompt is a reusable instruction that shapes how the model responds \u2014 for example, \u201CYou are a concise science tutor. Explain ideas clearly with everyday examples\u201D or \u201CYou are a senior code reviewer. Point out bugs, edge cases, and security issues.\u201D Create and manage them in Settings \u2192 System Prompts, then apply one to your chat. They are stored on your device and sent only to the local model.
What are tools and which ones are available?

Tools let capable models take actions during a reply. Three are available: Run JavaScript (math, dates, and text processing in an on-device sandbox), Web search (finds current information on the web), and Fetch web page (reads a page so the model can summarize or quote it). Turn them on in Settings \u2192 Tools. Each is off by default and works only with models that support tool calling \u2014 look for the hammer badge in the model selector.
Do the web tools send my data online?

Only when you enable them. Web search sends the model\'s query to DuckDuckGo, and Fetch web page downloads the pages the model chooses to open \u2014 those requests go to the websites themselves, not to the developer. Run JavaScript stays entirely on your device with no internet access. With every tool off (the default), nothing leaves your device. See the Privacy Policy for details.
Will the app notify me when a response is ready?

Yes. While the app is in the background, a notification tracks the model\'s status \u2014 loaded, generating, then response ready \u2014 and lets you copy or share the reply. You can also enable a short completion chime in Settings \u2192 Sound and Haptic. Model downloads show their own progress notification with speed and ETA.
Does voice dictation send my voice anywhere?

No. Tap the microphone in the chat input and speak \u2014 a speech-recognition model turns your words into text on your phone as you talk, in 35 languages. The audio is never saved or sent anywhere, so dictation works fully offline. The model (718 MB) downloads once, the first time you use the microphone.

Machine learning is a branch of artificial intelligence where computers **learn from data** instead of being explicitly programmed.

Key concepts:

• **Training**: feeding data to algorithms
• **Models**: learned patterns from data
• **Inference**: making predictions on new data
